title: Uninitialised variables start at zero
statement: A variable that has been declared but never assigned holds zero, or an empty value, so it can be safely read or added to.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: predict the outcome of reading a declared but unassigned local variable
evidence_patterns.signature: predicts 0 or empty output rather than a compile error or garbage value

example.expected: Compile error: count might not have been initialized

discriminators.vs_slip: A slip is forgetting one initialisation while knowing it is needed. The belief is stated ('it starts at zero') and the learner omits initialisation habitually.

conflicts_with.label: A variable has no usable value until it is assigned

resolved_by.label: A variable has no usable value until it is assigned

sources.citation: Chiodini, L., Moreno Santos, I., Gallidabino, A., Tafliovich, A., Santos, A. L., & Hauswirth, M. (2021). A curated inventory of programming language misconceptions. In Proceedings of the 26th ACM Conference on Innovation and Technology in Computer Science Education (ITiCSE '21), 380-386.
